title: Private VPC ops capacity sandbox notes — 2026
body:
Purpose and context:
This is a working sandbox doc for exploring mixed-hardware private/VPC capacity scenarios and quick BOM sketches. Goal: produce 3 plausible procurement scenarios (baseline / performance / bursty-reserve) that a customer-run private VPC could use as a starting point for an internal SOW. Not a final budget — focus on operational assumptions, utilization tradeoffs, and notes for the infra team to convert to a formal sizing sheet.

High-level assumptions (shared across scenarios):
- Target customer profile: mid-enterprise ML team, latency-sensitive chat features, daytime traffic peaks tied to NA/EU business hours.
- Baseline targeted steady-state 99th latency SLO: 350ms for small chat generations (<=512 tokens).
- Average request size: 256 tokens (prompt+reply), median sequence length 180 tokens; peak sequences occasionally hit 1024 tokens (<2% of traffic).
- Requests per second (average): 120 rps; peak burst handled by autoscale/burst: 650 rps sustained for 6 minutes (traffic bursts).
- Model: customer chooses a 30B-ish open model quantized to q4* equivalent with an inference footprint that fits on 80GB GPU for good latency profiles. For heavy-regression scenarios we also consider a 70B serving variant (needs H100 80GB or equivalent).

Key metrics to drive compute count: tokens/sec per GPU, concurrency capacity per GPU, KV cache impact, and batching efficiency. We use conservative throughput numbers derived from internal bench:
- 80GB H100 (perf tuned): ~220 tokens/sec (latency-focused interactive load, concurrency 12)
- 40GB A100 (dense q4/INT8 path): ~140 tokens/sec (concurrency 8)
- L40s-type (inference-optimized, 48GB): ~180 tokens/sec (concurrency 10)
Note: numbers are workload-dependent — include 15% overhead safety.

Quick throughput calcs (baseline target):
- Avg tokens/sec required = average_rps * avg_tokens = 120 * 256 = 30,720 tokens/sec
- Effective tokens/sec per mixed-GPU fleet (weighted): choose 6 x H100 + 8 x A100 as a starting mix -> capacity = 6*220 + 8*140 = 1320 + 1120 = 2440 tokens/sec -> clearly insufficient for this naive mapping, so we must compute proper scale.

Scenario sketches (high level):
1) Conservative baseline (cost-conscious, moderate latency):
   - Hardware mix: 24 x A100-40GB nodes (single GPU per host, on-prem rack optimized)
   - Effective capacity = 24 * 140 * 0.85 (operational safety) = 2856 tokens/sec -> still short of target 30720 tokens/sec.
   - Result: need roughly 215 A100 GPUs to meet token throughput if only A100 used (30720 / (140*0.85) ≈ 258 -> math shows gap; re-evaluate below with more realistic per-GPU tokens/sec under batching-heavy scenarios).
   - Tradeoffs: cheaper per-GPU unit cost but much larger rack footprint, higher networking and power.

2) Performance tier (latency + smaller footprint):
   - Hardware mix: 40 x H100-80GB (inference-optimized), 10 x L40s for mid-size routing.
   - Effective capacity ≈ 40*220*0.85 + 10*180*0.85 = 7480 + 1530 = 9010 tokens/sec -> still below peak but better.
   - To reach the 30k tokens/sec baseline, this scenario needs ~138 H100-equivalents (or a hybrid scaling with batching and request shaping).

3) Burst-reserve hybrid (on-prem steady + cloud-burst):
   - On-prem: 30 x H100-equivalents to cover steady-state (30*220*0.85 = 5610 tokens/sec)
   - Cloud-burst: allow rapid on-demand cloud pools for peak minutes (auto-provision up to +18000 tokens/sec) to hit 30k target.
   - Pros: lower capex, predictable steady op; Cons: cross-cloud networking, warm-up latency for cold GPUs, and potential data movement concerns for private deployments.

Why the large gaps?
- Our baseline tokens/sec target (30k) equates to ~140 concurrent full-token-decoding streams at 200 tokens/sec each, but interactive workloads have many short contexts and underutilized batch windows. The real lever is increasing batching + prefix caching to reduce per-token compute.

Small ASCII capacity table (illustrative)
"""
Compute type | count | tokens/sec (per) | eff (0.85) | total tokens/sec
-------------|-------|-------------------|-----------|-----------------
H100-80GB    | 40    | 220               | 187       | 7480
A100-40GB    | 24    | 140               | 119       | 2856
L40s         | 10    | 180               | 153       | 1530
TOTAL (example)                              = 11866 tokens/sec
"""

BOM rough cost sketch (unit costs are placeholders for discussion, include non-GPU items):
- H100-80GB GPU card: $55,000 (unit)
- A100-40GB GPU card: $20,000 (unit)
- Node chassis + CPU + NICs + NVMe + PSU + rack: $12,000 (per single-GPU server)
- 100GbE switch port + cabling: $2,500 (per port)
- Rack (42U) + PDU + basic install: $20,000
- Power + cooling (5-year estimate, per rack): $45,000

Example BOM line (performance tier):
- 40 x H100 cards = 40 * 55,000 = $2,200,000
- 40 x single-gpu chassis = 40 * 12,000 = $480,000
- Switching (48-port 100GbE) + spares = $120,000
- Racks (3x 42U) + PDUs = $60,000
- Installation/ops contingency (10%) = ~$286,000
- Estimated CAPEX (hardware + network + ops) ≈ $3.146M (5-year TCO excludes real estate and ongoing power at scale)

Operational items to model (included in next-sheet work):
- GPU utilization smoothing via KV prefix caching (expected 10–30% token reduction for chat workloads)
- Pre-warming vs cold-start tradeoffs for large models (warm workers held idle cost)
- Scheduling headroom: keep 20–30% spare to allow rolling upgrades and node failures without SLO impact
- Network saturation points: 100Gbps NIC per H100 node may saturate under multi-tenant batching — plan for 1.5x NIC capacity for heavy KV/caching traffic

Risk register (short list):
- Procurement delays on H100 leading to multi-month lead time — mitigation: staggered orders, mix with A100/L40
- Power constraints at customer site — mitigation: early electrical survey, modular PDUs
- Regulatory concerns for cloud-burst approach — mitigation: encrypted KV-only bursts, token-level redaction, legal signoff

Open questions / action items:
- Q1: confirm exact model family customer plans to serve (30B vs 70B) — impacts GPU choice and mem footprint (R: Elena)
- Q2: do we have accurate per-GPU tokens/sec numbers for our optimized runtime on L40s? Need bench run using customer prompts (R: Soham)
- Q3: rooftop vs colocation options for East US: gather power-density quotes (R: Jun)
- Prep: create a follow-up sheet with param-driven calculator where inputs are: average RPS, avg tokens, peak multiplier, desired 99p latency, batching efficiency (0.6–0.95), KV cache hit rate. Output: GPU counts by family, racks, prelim CAPEX and 5-year OPEX.

Notes to infra team (implementation specifics):
- When converting to a formal workbook, capture formulas as cell expressions and expose a mode to toggle batching assumptions; ship two tabs: 'steady-state only' and 'hybrid-burst plan'.
- Add columns for: power draw per server (idle vs full), estimated cooling load (kW), and real-estate rack units consumed.
- Add a sensitivity chart showing CAPEX vs peak multiplier and utilization (x-axis utilization 30–90% -> y-axis CAPEX per effective token/sec).

Next steps (timeline):
- Week 1: bench runs for target model flavors on L40/H100 (Soham)
- Week 2: initial paramized spreadsheet + CAPEX sketch (Marcus)
- Week 3: review with solutions engineering and SREs to validate rack/power networking assumptions (Elena/Jun)

Quick-contact references:
- Slack: #private-deployments, DM Marcus/Elena for clarifications
- Confluence: CONFLUENCE-DEPLOY-1234 (project page)
- Jira: JIRA-PRIVDEP-789 (capacity epic)

This doc intentionally mixes rough numbers and operational notes. The attached follow-up will be a dedicated sheet (param-driven) that converts these assumptions into deterministic GPU counts and a BOM with line-item pricing + power/OPEX columns. For now, this sandbox is to align on the right levers (batching, KV caching, hybrid burst) before we commit to a procurement profile.
